rationale: C11 is the expressly referenced July 6, 1960 Cuban sugar-quota proclamation and supplies the child’s concrete drafting framework. Both instruments construe the same section 408(b), make a national-interest determination fixing Cuba’s sugar quota for a specified period, use the same two-part operative sequence, place the Agriculture Secretary’s authority under State Department concurrence, and provide for immediate effectiveness upon Federal Register publication. The child adapts C11 by setting the next period’s quota to zero and continuing rather than initially making the delegation. C08 and C07 concern agricultural import quotas, but their different statutory machinery and operative structures make them substantially weaker.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I find it to be in the national interest that the amount of the quotas for sugar and for liquid sugar for Cuba ... for the three-month period ending March 31, 1961, should be zero
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I find it to be in the national interest that the quota for Cuba ... for the balance of calendar year 1960 shall be 39,752 short tons, raw value
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts the parent’s national-interest finding under the same statute to a new quota period and amount.

shared_material.child_excerpt: 1. Do hereby determine that in the national interest the amount of the quotas ... for Cuba ... shall be zero
shared_material.parent_excerpt: 1. Do hereby determine that in the national interest the quota for Cuba ... shall be 39,752 short tons, raw value
shared_material.explanation: The first numbered operative provision is a direct linguistic and functional template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: 2. Do hereby continue the delegation to the Secretary of Agriculture of the authority vested in the President by section 408(b) (2) and section 408(b) (3) ... such authority to be continued to be exercised with the concurrence of the Secretary of State.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: 2. Do hereby delegate to the Secretary of Agriculture the authority vested in the President by section 408(b) (2) and section 408(b) (3) ... such authority to be exercised with the concurrence of the Secretary of State.
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the parent’s second operative provision almost verbatim, changing the initial delegation into its continuation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: This proclamation shall become effective immediately upon publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: This proclamation shall become effective immediately upon publication in the FEDERAL REGISTER
shared_material.explanation: The same statute-specific immediate-effectiveness clause completes the parallel drafting structure.
